title: Redwood POC weekly sync - Quantaco AI - cost econ

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-01
Time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Ethan Carter (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Quantaco Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Quantaco SRE), Priya Shah (Quantaco Product), Jonas Keller (Ops)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call then we'll dive into the cost econ review. Ethan and I will run through the numbers we pulled from last week's run and Marco you said you'd have the staging replay results?
[00:18] Marco: Yep, we pushed a 24 hour replay over the weekend, got token counts and latency hist, some noise but overall usable.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool, i'll share my screen in a sec, but high-level - we compared 3 model variants: Llama-3-70B q8, Llama-3-70B q4, and a trimmed 13B q4 for tail queries. We measured tokens/sec and calculated tokens/sec per dollar using your committed dedicated price and our hosted estimates.
[01:05] Lena: Quick question - when you say tokens/sec per dollar, what's the exact formula? Are you normalizing to per-GPU-hour cost or total spend across cluster?
[01:18] Ethan: Good call. We're normalizing to per-hour GPU cost. So tokens/sec/$ means tokens per second divided by hourly cost in dollars, effectively tokens/sec per dollar of hourly GPU cost. It's a shorthand we used for comparison.
[01:36] Priya: Slightly odd unit but as long as it's consistent between variants it's fine.
[01:45] Ethan: Right. Numbers: baseline (no prefix cache, small batching) Llama-3-70B q8 ~1,200 tokens/sec on a single node @ $6.50/hr equivalent -> ~184 tokens/sec/$; q4 on same hw gave ~1,900 tokens/sec -> ~292 tokens/sec/$; 13B q4 ~3,800 tokens/sec -> ~584 tokens/sec/$. Those are median throughput numbers from our runs.
[02:25] Jonas: Wait, 13B gives way more tokens/sec/$, is that because of smaller model size or memory fit so fewer stalls?
[02:37] Ethan: Exactly, smaller model fits better in the kernel paths, fewer memory ops. But accuracy for your prompt mixes drops slightly - we surfaced eval differences in the spreadsheet.
[02:55] Marco: The replay showed q4 reduced compute by roughly 40% vs q8 for similar latencies.
[03:10] Maya: Now caching - we looked at prefix/KV cache on at 80% cache hit expected. With cache enabled, effective tokens that need full model compute dropped by 35% across your conversational flows. That translated to an estimated cost reduction of ~28% overall in the pilot run.
[03:40] Lena: How confident are we about 80% hit? Our prefix variability is high for multi-turns.
[03:50] Marco: On staging we measured ~72% average, spikes down to 60 at peak. The 80 number was our optimistic target. The replay traffic has fewer niche queries, so prod might be lower.
[04:06] Ethan: We recommended config changes: increase cache TTL for mid-sessions, and do smarter prefix hashing to boost hits. Also we saw that KV cache helps more for 70B because repeated system+instruction prefixes are heavy.
[04:28] Priya: Okay - batching tradeoffs? We saw some docs where batching gave big throughput but increased tail latency. We care about 95th latency under 1s.
[04:40] Ethan: Right. In our tests, small batching (batch size 8) increased throughput by ~1.6x and added ~80ms to median, but 95th went from 720ms to 1.1s. Large batching (32) pushed throughput 3x but 95th hit 2.2s. So trade is clear: throughput vs tail latency.
[05:08] Marco: On dedicated pools we can reserve low-latency lanes (smaller batches) for critical traffic and a high-throughput lane for bulk scoring.
[05:20] Lena: That will complicate routing, but doable. We need cost per route breakdown in the spreadsheet.
[05:29] Maya: We'll add per-route tokens/sec and approximate cost given expected traffic mix.
[05:35] Ethan: Also quantization: q4 gave ~35-40% cost reduction compared to q8 in our runs, but we also measured a small regression in some of your NLU intents - around a 2-3% accuracy delta on edge cases.
[05:55] Lena: 2-3% might be fine for non-critical responses, but for high-value transactions we want calf checks.
[06:05] Priya: We should do hybrid routing: use 13B or q4 for chatty flows and 70B q4 for critical intents.
[06:15] Ethan: Exactly, that's a recommended approach - route by intent confidence and user segment.
[06:22] [08:00] Ethan: I threw the detailed numbers in the spreadsheet - pages 2-4 show tokens/sec, hourly cost assumptions, and projected monthly spend at your 10M tokens/day baseline. With current traffic, switching to q4+cache yields projected saving of ~32% month-over-month.
[08:40] Marco: The replay data lines up with that projection, we saw cost delta in the same ballpark when we simulate the traffic. But getting prefix cache into prod safely is our blocker.
[09:02] Maya: On the cache rollout plan: start with 20% traffic, validate accuracy and latency, then ramp. Ethan, can you provide a safe ramp playbook?
[09:12] Ethan: Yup - playbook includes canary at 5%, A/B compare latency and token counts, health checks and auto-rollback if 95th latency increases >250ms or error rate rises >0.5%. We'll add those thresholds to the doc.
[09:30] Jonas: Also need to ensure cache invalidation for prompt template changes - we can't serve stale system prompts.
[09:40] Ethan: We'll make TTLs explicit and provide hooks for manual invalidation via API.
[10:00] [15:00] Marco: One thing we noticed - KV cache metadata causes small memory bloat on nodes with many open sessions. For dedicated we can size nodes accordingly but for hosted we'd need guardrails.
[15:20] Maya: Good note. We'll include recommended instance profiles for expected concurrency.
[15:30] Lena: Back to tokens/sec/$ - can you reframe as cost per 1M tokens? Exec team asks for $/1M tokens not tokens/sec/$.
[15:45] Ethan: Sure. Using the hourly cost and throughput, rough numbers: Llama-70B q8 ~ $28 / 1M tokens; q4 ~ $17 / 1M tokens; 13B q4 ~ $8.5 / 1M tokens. With prefix cache applied at current hit rates, effective $/1M drops by ~25% across the board.
[16:20] Priya: Great, that's easier to digest. Put those in the top of the spreadsheet.
[16:30] Ethan: Will do.
[16:35] [22:00] Lena: Any security or compliance issues with caching? Our security team flagged persistence of sensitive prefixes.
[22:10] Maya: We support configurable cache encryption at rest and KMS integration for keys. You can also exclude user-sensitive prompts from caching via match rules. We'll share the security doc link.
[22:30] Marco: We'll need audit logs for cache hits and invalidations - that's part of our compliance ask.
[22:38] Ethan: Redwood console exposes per-request traces and cache hit logs; we'll map fields to your audit schema.
[22:50] Priya: On the SLA - what latency tiers can we guarantee on dedicated?
[22:58] Ethan: With reserved capacity and small batch lanes we can target 95th < 900ms for typical chat queries; for strict 500ms you'd need smaller models or more reserved nodes which increases cost. We'll model both.
[23:20] Maya: Ok, let's capture both a latency-optimized and cost-optimized run in the spreadsheet.
[23:28] [30:00] Marco: Quick note on orchestration - when switching model variants we saw a bump in cold-starts due to kernel preload. We can pre-warm pipelines on rotation to avoid tail spikes.
[30:15] Ethan: We have pre-warm hooks in Redwood Dedicated to maintain a hot model instance for minimal cold starts. We'll show expected extra cost for that in the calc.
[30:30] Lena: Sounds good.
[30:35] [36:00] Priya: Let's align on success criteria for the pilot: reduce monthly inference spend by >20% while maintaining <2% accuracy regression on top intents and keeping 95th latency under 1s for customer-facing chat. Does that look right?
[36:18] Maya: Sounds reasonable. We'll put that as the working success criteria.
[36:28] Lena: We'll bring this to the execs after you update the spreadsheet.
[36:35] Maya: Final quick recaps and owners - Ethan will run kernel perf tests and update cost model; Marco will enable cache on staging and run replay; Maya will send security docs and a proposed rollout playbook.
[36:55] Ethan: I'll also capture the per-route cost breakdown and suggested routing rules (critical vs bulk).
[37:05] Jonas: I'll validate the ops sizing numbers and confirm concurrency targets.
[37:15] [44:00] Maya: Great, thanks everyone. We'll aim to have the updated spreadsheet and playbook by Friday. Next sync same time next week unless we need the kernel deep dive earlier.
[44:20] Lena: Thanks, bye.
